review_notes: I read the whole file and the FundamentalGroupoid/Basic.lean simp conventions (natIsoMk with @[simps!], mapFundamentalGroupoid_obj_mk and map_homMk as @[simp]). I grepped Mathlib for uses of the congrMapFundamentalGroupoid and diagOfSimplicialObjectHomotopy_edge lemmas; the only uses are in this file. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether simp would close the goals in the proposed form or whether the extra simp lemmas would change other simp calls. I found no loop or competing-rule problem. The two findings are about missing simp lemmas, and they are moderate-confidence.

findings.excerpt:
lemma congrMapFundamentalGroupoid_hom_app_mk (h : Homotopy f g) (x : X _⦋0⦌) :
    (congrMapFundamentalGroupoid h).hom.app (.mk x) =
findings.problem: These two lemmas are the canonical component formulas for the isomorphisms. They rewrite an opaque application `(congrMapFundamentalGroupoid h).hom.app (mk x)` to `homMk (Edge.ofSimplicialObjectHomotopy ..)`. Neither is tagged `@[simp]`, although the matching component lemmas in Basic.lean are (`mapFundamentalGroupoid_obj_mk`, `mapFundamentalGroupoid_map_homMk`). Since `congrMapFundamentalGroupoid` is a plain noncomputable def, simp has no way to unfold it, so users must cite these lemmas by name. The right-hand side is built from `homMk` and `Edge.ofSimplicialObjectHomotopy`, which are already simp-normal, and no other simp rule rewrites the left-hand side. Tagging them looks safe: there is no looping risk and no competing rule.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to both `congrMapFundamentalGroupoid'_hom_app_mk` and `congrMapFundamentalGroupoid_hom_app_mk`. Optionally also add `@[simp]` to an `inv_app_mk` variant, stated as `inv (homMk ..)`. Then `simp` can reduce component expressions at `mk x` to `homMk (Edge.ofSimplicialObjectHomotopy ..)`, which `comm_of_ofSimplicialObjectHomotopy` and `mapFundamentalGroupoid_map_homMk` can then use.
findings.benefit: Downstream proofs about homotopy-induced natural isomorphisms (for example naturality or invariance statements) can use `simp` directly. They won't need to cite these `rfl` lemmas by hand, which matches how the neighbouring Basic.lean component lemmas are used.

findings.excerpt:
lemma diagOfSimplicialObjectHomotopy_edge :
    (diagOfSimplicialObjectHomotopy h e).edge = Y.δ 1 (h.h 1 e.edge) := by rfl
findings.problem: The sibling projection lemma `ofSimplicialObjectHomotopy_edge` is `@[simp]`. The two projection lemmas for the `@[no_expose]` def `diagOfSimplicialObjectHomotopy` have no simp attribute, and `diagOfSimplicialObjectHomotopy_edge` is the only way to see through the definition. They are passed by name to `simp [...]` at lines 116 and 127. This is an incomplete simp interface: it is unclear which of the two forms is meant to be canonical, and `.edge` of the diagonal stays opaque to `simp`. The two lemmas have the same left-hand side but different right-hand sides (`h.h 1` versus `h.h 0`). Making both simp would give competing rules, and one of them would have to be chosen as the normal form.
findings.proposed_change: Make `diagOfSimplicialObjectHomotopy_edge` the canonical `@[simp]` lemma, since it matches the definition. Add a docstring or comment saying that `_edge'` is a non-simp alternative form, to be passed explicitly to `simp [...]`. This also lets the `simp [diagOfSimplicialObjectHomotopy_edge]` call at line 116 drop its explicit argument. Keep `_edge'` unannotated so the two don't compete.
findings.benefit: The simp set becomes consistent with `ofSimplicialObjectHomotopy_edge`. It gives one documented normal form for the diagonal edge's underlying simplex. Proofs about the `CompStruct`s no longer need to name the lemma explicitly, and readers can tell which form is canonical.
